plan.hypothesis: On the historical T0 fixed-radius structure executed with the fixed controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0, raising control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight above its 0.05 nominal toward its 0.1 upper bound will suppress the held-window tip speed below the 0.02 m/s acceptance bound while keeping terminal error and holding position inside 0.01 m, converting the recorded near-miss valid failure into joint nominal reach-and-hold acceptance with force bounds intact and a finite valid execution, without any structural change.
plan.rationale: Control-only research is legitimate and the two tip-speed weights are the only legal continuous control paths. The prior batch was flagged as a repetition because its v2-T2 source already ran under controller10; switching to the historical T0 fixed-radius (executed only with controller9) makes every batch point a new scientific configuration under the fixed controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0, with the base re-established and its replication purpose declared. The intervention is directly indicated: T0 already meets terminal error and holding position and misses only held tip speed, so the single increasable lever, holding_tip_speed_weight, is the right target. Coordinate search with fractional step 0.5 over [0.05,0.1] keeps the base and one upward proposal, never reusing any old cross-template routing scale, and at most two new backend attempts preserve the six-execution development budget. Every point must yield a complete evaluation with force bounds and a finite valid execution before any joint-acceptance claim. Should a new candidate be selected for joint acceptance, one exact fresh verification would be required, with a second contemporary reference only for a comparative claim.

arguments.reasoning: Feedback first: the current exact feedback is F602 (status='engineering_feedback') with F598 (stop_reason='known_scientific_point_requires_repetition_purpose') - the prior batch was judged to re-execute a known scientific point without a repetition purpose. That prior batch branched from v2-T2, whose saved V2 execution already used controller10, so a coordinate search anchored there re-touches a known configuration. I therefore move the supported source to the historical T0 fixed-radius (incumbent/retained comparison), whose only completed execution used controller 9.0.0; under the fixed controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0 every batch point is a new scientific configuration, and the coordinate base at holding_tip_speed_weight=0.05 is re-established explicitly with a replication_reason because exact historical reuse is impossible. T0 is also the strongest source on the joint objective: its held position and terminal error already satisfy the acceptance bounds (F284=0.00336 m < 0.01 m) and it misses only held tip speed (F28=0.02682 m/s > 0.02 m/s), whereas v2-T1/v2-T2 are far worse (F187=0.01109 m terminal, F1=0.02342 m held position, F224=1.12102 m/s held speed) and still fail jointly (F192=false, F3='valid_failure'). The only legal and increasable control lever is holding_tip_speed_weight (F497=0.05, domain [0.025,0.1]); terminal_tip_speed_weight is already pinned at its 0.1 upper bound (F354) and cannot be raised. Candidate-local bounded_endpoint for T2 reports locally feasible controller-start and target points (F567, F561), but that is a local affine witness only, not a nonlinear certificate, so it does not establish that the T2 miss is physical. Hence a bounded coordinate search over holding_tip_speed_weight on the T0 fixed-radius structure under controller10 is the best-supported control-only step toward joint reach-and-hold acceptance.
